The Swift finished-nights filter is inline in the excluded app layer; the Kotlin function is a separate test seam, so this records a role twin only.

Swift Repository.hrFingerprintUnion computes the same repository witness role, but the implementations encode the facts differently and have no byte-identity contract.

Twin of the Swift UserProfile.cacheKey, which lives with the Swift UserProfile in Packages/StrandAnalytics/Sources/StrandAnalytics/WorkoutDetector.swift; the two types sit in differently named files, so the ledger cannot pair them.
Twin of the Kotlin UserProfile.cacheKey in android/app/src/main/java/com/noop/analytics/AnalyticsModels.kt; the two types sit in differently named files, so the ledger cannot pair them.

Twin of the Kotlin `val OuraSpO2.channel` in android/app/src/main/java/com/noop/oura/OuraEvents.kt. Both are one-line extension properties over OuraSpO2 returning OuraSpO2Channel, added together in the same change. Kotlin declares its copy as a TOP-LEVEL extension property with a dotted receiver, which the ledger's Kotlin property scan does not index, so the Swift side reads as one-sided. The pair is real; only one half is visible to the inventory.

Room @Query DAO method. The Swift store issues the equivalent SQL inline in WhoopStore Reads.swift / StreamStore.swift rather than through a DAO, so there is no Swift function to pair with; its WHOOP 5 siblings whoop5RrIntervals, hasWhoop5RrSource and promoteWhoop5RrSource are one-sided for the same architectural reason.

Room @Query DAO method (#2371). The Swift store runs the same statement inline in WhoopStore StreamStore.swift rather than through a DAO, so there is no Swift function to pair with; the SQL itself is paired, WHOOP5_RR_FILL_FLAG_SQL with WhoopStore.whoop5RrFillFlagSQL, and pinned by the same literal on both platforms.

Room Migration.migrate override of MIGRATION_40_41 (#2371). GRDB registers each migration as a closure (`v47-rr-whoop5-fill`), so there is no Swift function to pair with; the two are paired by the migration identifiers pinned in schema_oracle.json and by the SQL constant pair WHOOP5_RR_FILL_MIGRATION_SQL / WhoopStore.whoop5RrFillMigrationSQL.

SQL text for a Room @Query, which must be a compile-time constant string and so cannot be inlined at the DAO method. The Swift store writes the same statement inline in WhoopStore Reads.swift / StreamStore.swift, so there is no Swift constant to pair with, exactly as for the existing WHOOP5_RR_INTERVALS_SQL and PROMOTE_WHOOP5_RR_SOURCE_SQL siblings.

Consumed only by the Apple OuraLiveSource screen-off live-HR suspend (Experimental "All-day heart rate & HRV"), to stand the daytime-HR hold down for the learned night instead of for every screen-off. Android's OuraLiveSource.kt has no screen-off suspend (#1546), so there is nothing for a Kotlin twin to gate; per review, Android stays without it until that suspend exists, at which point this becomes a twin.

The added preserveUnscoredHistory argument matches the role of analyzeRecent in the excluded Swift app layer. This records the new Kotlin orchestration signature, not a byte-identity claim.
The additional HR input feeds offWristIntervals during Android stream preparation; Swift performs the corresponding read and wear reconciliation inline in the excluded app-layer analyzeRecent.

The shared repair delegates to the scorer with cached-only preservation. Swift runEffortRescoreIfNeeded/runHistoryRepairIfNeeded perform that role in the excluded app layer; signatures differ by platform dependencies.

Swift groups daily metrics, metric points and provenance by day inline in app-layer analyzeRecent. Kotlin extracts that persistence preparation as a test seam; this is a role twin, not a function parity claim.
Swift IntelligenceEngine.historyRepairIsPending has the same repair-flag gate in the excluded app layer; both have direct truth-table coverage.
Swift app-layer analyzeRecent performs the conditional per-day persistence loop inline. Kotlin extracts it to keep the instrumented scoring coroutine below the bytecode budget.

This Kotlin extension dispatches a computed window to repository persistence. The corresponding persistComputedScores dispatch is inline in the excluded Swift app-layer analyzeRecent; this records its architectural role.
The Swift app engine captures the same per-pass build stamp in its currentComputationStamp method; Strand/ is outside the governed Swift roots.
Kotlin extracts the weekly fitness/vitality/steps persistence from the scoring coroutine; the corresponding pass is inline in the excluded Swift app engine.
Kotlin constructs the stamped computed window in a helper; Swift assembles the same daily, metric, and source rows inline in the excluded app engine.
Room requires an annotated DAO delete for the new device-scoped table. Swift deletes the table inline through DeviceRegistryStore.deviceScopedTables rather than through a DAO.
Room requires a separate annotated DAO update during device identity adoption. Swift iterates its device-scoped tables and rekeys this table inline.
Room needs materialized entity rows before its batch @Upsert. Swift deduplicates and writes the corresponding cells inline in WhoopStore.persistComputedScores.
Room expresses the score-window deletion as an annotated DAO query. Swift issues the scoped DELETE inline in WhoopStore.persistComputedScores.
This is the Room Migration_41_42 override for Android schema 42. Swift registers the analogous table in a GRDB v48 migration closure, with different platform versioning.
Android repository forwards this call to the Room DAO transaction. Swift WhoopStore exposes the transaction directly; that substantive transaction is paired with the DAO method.
